results: 1. Comprehensive neurological examination, including eye movements, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural stability, pull test, gait initiation, turning, tandem gait, dual-task gait, cerebellar testing, sensory examination, reflexes, and plantar responses
muscle tone examination: symmetric neck and limb rigidity
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: brisk reflexes; normal plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: retropulsion; recovers in 2-3 steps
vertical saccades and gaze range (up and down): full
smooth pursuit and saccade velocity: normal
pull test / retropulsion: recovers in 2-3 steps
gait observation including turning and doorways: not recorded
freezing-of-gait provocation (doorway, turning, dual task): start hesitation and freezing, worst on turning and on passing through a doorway; MDS-UPDRS III 35, Hoehn and Yahr 2.5
limb rigidity and axial (neck) rigidity: SYMMETRIC rigidity of neck and limbs with mild symmetric bradykinesia and NO tremor
finger tapping for bradykinesia and decrement: normal
cerebellar testing (dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, tandem gait): normal
2. MRI of the brain with and without contrast, including diffusion-weighted, FLAIR, susceptibility-weighted, and sagittal midline sequences
MRI brain with gadolinium: progressive bilateral caudate and putaminal necrotic lesions without specific enhancement
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: bilateral caudate and putaminal restricted diffusion
MRI susceptibility-weighted sequences: normal
MRI brain - midbrain (hummingbird sign, midbrain-to-pons ratio): normal midbrain, ratio within normal limits

MRI brain - putamen (atrophy, rim sign, hot cross bun, SWI hypointensity): BILATERAL PUTAMEN AND CAUDATE hyperintensity on T2 and FLAIR with patchy restricted diffusion suggesting NECROSIS, and T1 hyperintensity in the ventral putamen; the lesions progressed over serial scans
MRI brain - cortical atrophy pattern: no focal atrophy
MRI brain - white matter and ventricles (small-vessel disease, ventriculomegaly): normal

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease, striatal-predominant (MM2-striatal) prion disease causing bilateral caudate–putaminal degeneration and parkinsonism

ALTERNATIVE 1: Toxic bilateral striatal necrosis, particularly carbon-monoxide or methanol-induced injury

ALTERNATIVE 2: Adult-onset mitochondrial striatal degeneration (Leigh-spectrum disease)

ALTERNATIVE 3: Wilson disease with atypical bilateral striatal involvement
